$comment: The 2411 cutover measurement. check:layover-cutover's NON_VACUITY condition consumes this, because 2411 declares no schema object — its whole effect is a row count, and a row count is OPERATIONAL DATA that no static check can establish. The migration's own header carries a hand measurement; the checker refuses prose as evidence, and this file is the answer to that refusal. COUNTS AND SHAPES ONLY: no titles, no cities, no ids, nothing that could identify a traveller or a place, because this file is committed and read in a diff.
method: read-only SELECTs over public.layover_recommendations, layover_plan_stops, feature_flags and information_schema.columns, issued through the Supabase Management API in an authorised session. The exact predicate is printed VERBATIM by `node --import tsx/esm src/scripts/emitLayoverCutoverSql.ts`, which builds it from 2411's own CASE expression rather than from a retyped copy — the query that produced these numbers and the query in the repository are the same text.
verdictWhy: 30 row(s) would receive a key, but 0 are moderated and 0 are referenced by a plan stop — nothing measured depends on their ids surviving the cutover sweep.
$reading: 2411 exists to keep an admin's moderation status alive across the cutover sweep. Production holds 30 layover_recommendations, every one of them status='active' and every one of them unkeyed, across 5 sessions, newest 30 days old. There are ZERO layover_plan_stops in the entire table, so nothing references any recommendation id at all — and that FK is ON DELETE SET NULL in any case. So the backfill would write 30 keys and preserve NOTHING: no moderation state, no plan-stop reference. It is not unsafe (0 ambiguous derivations, 0 colliding keys, and both 2410 prerequisites present) and it is not a no-op (it would touch 30 rows). It is simply not needed for the thing it was written to do. That is what OPTIONAL means here, and it is deliberately not rounded up to REQUIRED to make applying it easier to justify.
$doesNotProve: This measurement does NOT establish that moderation restoration works, because there was no moderated row to restore. If a moderated legacy row ever exists, this artifact is stale and the question is open again — which is why legacyModerated is recorded rather than assumed, and why the checker treats legacyModerated = 0 as VACUOUS FOR ITS PURPOSE rather than as a clean bill.
$remeasured:
RE-RUN TWICE, never edited. The freshness rule — schemaWatermark behind the snapshot's productionMigrationWatermark — has now fired twice, and both times the QUERY WAS RE-RUN rather than the field bumped. Bumping it without re-reading is the exact substitution this artifact exists to prevent.

First re-run, at watermark 20260908073559, after 2540 and 2660: both index-only on trust_events, touching nothing counted here.

Second re-run, at watermark 20260908104255, after 2535, 2335 and 2510 — and this one was NOT a formality. 2335 acts on THIS TABLE: it replaced layover_recs_owner (FOR ALL, with_check NULL) with a FOR SELECT policy and narrowed the grants to authenticated=SELECT, service_role=SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, anon=nothing. A change to who may write the table is exactly the kind of thing that could have altered what is in it, so the counts were taken again rather than argued about. Every number is unchanged: total 30, legacy 30, legacy moderated 0, ambiguous 0, ambiguous moderated 0, colliding keys 0, plan stops on legacy rows 0, 5 distinct sessions, cutover flag FALSE, and both 2410 prerequisites (rec_key column, unique index) present. Verdict stays OPTIONAL.

One thing to state rather than leave implicit: the measurement is issued through the Management API, which connects as an owner role and therefore BYPASSES the RLS 2335 tightened. That is why the counts are comparable across the change at all — the query sees the same rows before and after — and it is also why this artifact says nothing about what an END-USER token can now read. 2510 is the file that asserts that, and it passes.
